title: Hydrogen-Deuterium Exchange Mass Spectrometry of the VPS13C-Calmodulin Complex
author: Matthew Parson
materials: Prepare 52 µL stock solutions containing 3 micromolar (µM) VPS13C-dATG2C-3xFLAG/CaM and either 6 millimolar (mM) EGTA or 6 millimolar (mM) Ca 2+ in Protein Buffer.
Incubate these stock solutions On ice for 01:00:00 .

steps.title: Thaw and Clarify Protein Stock
steps.instruction: Thaw the VPS13C‑dATG2C‑3xFLAG/CaM stock on ice, then centrifuge at 15 000 × g, 4 °C for 5 min to pellet any aggregates.

steps.title: Aliquot Protein into EGTA and Ca2+ Tubes
steps.instruction: Distribute 4 µL of each thawed stock into 0.6 mL micro‑centrifuge tubes, making 11 tubes for VPS13C/CaM + EGTA and 11 tubes for VPS13C/CaM + Ca²⁺; each tube contains 12 pmol protein.

steps.title: Prepare Deuterated Samples and Replicates
steps.instruction: Add 8 µL D₂O buffer to each 4 µL protein aliquot (final volume 12 µL, 56.7 % D₂O). Create all conditions and time‑points in triplicate, yielding 9 deuterated samples for EGTA (3 × 3 s, 3 × 30 s, 3 × 300 s) and 9 for Ca²⁺. Do not exceed 50 µL protein + D₂O buffer; total HDX sample volume will be adjusted to 70 µL with quench buffer as described later.

steps.title: Set Robot Temperature and Keep Needle Ice‑Cold
steps.instruction: Set the climate‑controlled chromatography system of the HDx‑3 PAL liquid‑handling robot to 2 °C and keep the sample‑injection needle on ice.

steps.title: Wash Injection Needle and Sample Loop
steps.instruction: Perform the following washes to prevent cross‑contamination:

substeps.instruction: Wash the injection needle 3 × 100 µL ice‑cold 0.1 % formic acid.
Wash the HDx‑3 PAL sample loop 3 × 100 µL ice‑cold 0.1 % formic acid.

steps.title: Inject Sample and Start UPLC/MS
steps.instruction: Rapidly thaw a single HDX sample, inject the full 12 µL volume into the washed sample loop, and immediately start the UPLC and MS protocols to minimize back‑exchange.

steps.title: Perform Exchange Reaction at 18 °C
steps.instruction: Run the exchange at 18 °C for the desired time‑point (3 s, 30 s, or 300 s) using the following timing tables (all times are minutes after the start of the protocol):

substeps.instruction: 3 s time‑point: Off‑ice 0:10, D₂O time 0:20, Quench time 0:23.
30 s time‑point (two replicates shown): Off‑ice 0:10, 0:30; D₂O time 0:20, 0:40; Quench time 0:50, 1:10.

steps.title: Quench Reaction and Freeze Samples
steps.instruction: Stop the exchange by adding 58 µL diluted ice‑cold acidic quench buffer (20 µL quench buffer + 38 µL de‑ionized water), giving a final volume of 70 µL with 0.6 M guanidine‑HCl, 0.9 % formic acid, pH 2.5. Immediately snap‑freeze in liquid nitrogen and store at –80 °C until MS analysis.

steps.title: Clean Injection Needle for Next Sample
Configure UPLC Flow and Mobile Phase
steps.instruction: Set the UPLC fluidics system to a flow rate of 200 µL/min using 0.05 % TFA as the mobile phase.

steps.title: Digest Sample on Pepsin Column
steps.instruction: Pass the quenched sample over an immobilized pepsin column (Affipro, AP‑PC‑001, 2.1 mm i.d. × 20 mm, 69.3 µL) at 2 °C for 4 min, then trap and desalt the resulting peptides on a UPLC BEH C18 pre‑column (Acquity, 186004629, 2.1 mm × 5 mm, 1.7 µm).

steps.title: Elute Peptides with Gradient
steps.instruction: Elute peptides from the C18 pre‑column onto a BEH C18 analytical column (Acquity, 186003686, 2.1 mm × 100 mm, 1.7 µm) using the following gradient of UPLC Buffer B:

substeps.instruction: Hold at 35 % B for 1 min 00 s.

steps.title: Acquire MS/MS Data with DDA
steps.instruction: Perform data‑dependent acquisition: 0.5 s precursor scan from 150–2000 m/z, followed by twelve 0.25 s fragment scans (150–2000 m/z). Acquire over a mass range of 150–2200 m/z using an electrospray ionization source set to 200 °C and 4.5 kV spray voltage.

steps.title: Identify Peptides and Prepare Sequencing Sample
steps.instruction: Identify peptides from non‑deuterated samples using the DDA data. Additionally, prepare a high‑concentration non‑deuterated MS/MS sequencing sample by mixing 10 µL of 3 µM VPS13C‑dATG2C‑3xFLAG/CaM with 60 µL diluted ice‑cold acidic quench buffer (20 µL quench buffer + 40 µL H₂O), yielding 30 pmol protein per sample.

steps.title: Analyze Data with HD‑Examiner and FragPipe
steps.instruction: Use HD‑Examiner (Trajan Scientific & Medical) to calculate deuterium incorporation for each peptide (automatic calculation plus manual inspection). Analyze MS/MS datasets with FragPipe v23.1 employing MSFragger with the following settings: precursor mass tolerance –20 to +20 ppm, fragment mass tolerance 20 ppm, nonspecific digestion, peptide length 4–50 aa, mass range 400–5000 Da. Use the Philosopher toolkit and search against databases of purified proteins, known contaminants, and E. coli/Sf9 contaminant databases.

steps.title: Flush Column with Buffer B
steps.instruction: Flush the analytical column with UPLC Buffer B before running the next sample.

steps.title: Deposit Data to ProteomeXchange PRIDE
steps.instruction: Deposit all proteomics data to the ProteomeXchange Consortium via the PRIDE partner repository.
